reasons: Classification is defensible: Section 13.1 creates a multi-year, Product-by-Product term running to expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term, and the only at-will exit (13.2) does not commence until a redacted period after First Commercial Sale of both the Binimetinib and Encorafenib Products, leaving the entire development/pre-launch phase with no Customer convenience right — which fails the fallback's material requirement of a Customer convenience exit during the term and matches the walk-away wording.
Vendor-side prong is correctly assessed as satisfied (Array's exits under 13.3/13.4/8.2 are for-cause), so the finding does not over-reach on that element.

Redline is directionally correct and actionable: deleting the commencement trigger and permitting termination at any time on ninety (90) days' notice reaches the fallback position, and the added 'in its entirety or on a Product-by-Product basis' tracks the model language's 'in whole or in part'.

Failed regex check ('Customer convenience termination present') is a phrasing variant — 'terminate this Agreement at any time ... for any reason' is substantively a convenience right — and the 0.664 changed-character ratio is explained by the need to rewrite the delayed-commencement trigger, so neither check undermines the substance.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, states what changed and why, and transparently flags acceptance of the 90-day fallback notice period.

Minor (non-fatal) points to tighten: the rationale says the redacted notice period 'should be confirmed at 30–90 days' while the redline unilaterally fixes it at 90 days — since the original period is redacted it could in fact have been shorter, so the edit should be framed as 'no more than ninety (90) days' or leave the redaction intact; the edit could also have been more minimal by deleting only the 'Commencing on the later of ...' lead-in.
